reason: A shrinks both decorative circles into floating discs that no longer bleed off the edges, so the original's look is lost; the top-right disc sits awkwardly next to the logo and can, the content is pushed into the top half, and a large empty band separates the CTA from the tiny legal line. B keeps the original's bleeding circles and gives the content a more balanced vertical position, but 'GLACIER' and the can's right side sit on the big circle, the legal line rides over the bottom-left circle and floats about 100px above the bottom edge, and the legal text is very small.

A: the SOLSTICE logo is tiny and jammed into the top-left corner, and the bottle cap nearly touches the top edge. The headline and copy cluster at the top centre and leave dead space underneath, so the hierarchy feels weak. B: the brand is legible and the headline-then-CTA order reads well, but it is cramped. The bottle spans almost the full height, the headline's 'fizz' runs into the muddy pair of overlapping circles, the copy wraps to 3 lines, and the oversized CTA crowds the right edge. Neither would ship; I picked B narrowly because its brand and hierarchy survive better.

A breaks the headline-to-CTA grouping: the CTA floats about 150px below the headline, near the canvas middle, and the bottom third is empty, so the layout looks top-heavy and unplanned. The headline is also small for the portrait canvas. B scales the headline up so it fills the format, rewraps it cleanly over four lines and keeps the CTA tight under it, which preserves the original's centered stack. Its flaw is vertical balance: the group sits low, with about 170px above it but only about 50px under the CTA, which crowds the bottom edge and needs polish.

A keeps a clean left-aligned column with logical order (logo→headline→sub→pills→CTA), but the headline wraps to leave an orphaned 'here', and the content sits jammed into the left 60% while the right half is dead space holding only a lone pink circle. B fills the canvas, but the alignment is ragged: the headline starts at x≈64 while the logo, subhead and pills start at x≈76. The oversized headline runs within about 30px of the right edge, the CTA floats off-grid on the right, and the flavour pills fall below the CTA, which breaks the reading order. The pink circle shrinks to a stray corner blob.

A keeps the product-in-circle graphic intact, but squeezes everything into the top 40% and leaves the bottom 60% as dead orange. The 'Try It' pill runs off the right edge and is jammed under the NEW badge, out of line with the copy. B spreads the content out, but it breaks the key graphic: the cream circle is cut away into a clipped blob in the bottom-left corner. That leaves the can as an orange-on-orange outline that almost disappears. The headline is also too small, and the NEW badge and CTA float on different axes from the text block.

A: the FREE ENTRY and ALL AGES pills overlap, and ALL AGES is cut off at the right edge. The missing-asset box crashes into the 'Saturday 21 June' line, and the legal text sits large in the middle of the canvas under the subhead. On the plus side, the RSVP button stays prominent. B: the big two-line headline anchors the left, but the RSVP button has shrunk to the size of the three tag pills, so the call to action is buried. The 'SOLSTICE' logo text looks broken ('SOLST CE'), the date has an awkward gap above its details, and the elements are scattered across four loose columns. B wins slightly because it has fewer hard collisions and nothing clipped.

A: the 'See the Schedule' button is jammed into the bottom-left corner, clipped by the canvas edge, and sits on top of the fine print, which is cut off ('...the café go to the local library fund'). The card also fills almost the whole canvas, so the confetti framing is lost. B: the book on the confetti beside a headline card reads well as a banner, and the CTA and fine print are grouped cleanly. Its flaws: the Inkwell & Lantern logo has shrunk to near-illegible size, the card runs tight to the right and top edges, and the book floats a little low with an uneven left margin.

A: the big teal circle is pulled fully inside the canvas, so the GLACIER logo and the can's right edge sit on it, which looks like a collision rather than layering. The legal line floats mid-canvas over the lower circle with about 100px of dead space below it, and there is a large empty band above the logo. B: the order logo → can → headline → CTA → legal matches the original and the legal sits at the bottom where it belongs, but the teal circle is visibly squashed into an ellipse and no longer bleeds off the edge. There is also about 200px of dead space between the CTA and the legal, which makes the content cluster top-heavy.

A reads left to right as a proper banner with a legible SOLSTICE wordmark and a dominant headline, but it is cramped: the two circles are piled behind the end of 'fizz', the CTA pill is oversized and jammed against the 3-line body copy and the right edge, and the bottle nearly touches the top and bottom edges. B shrinks the SOLSTICE logo to a tiny, barely legible mark stuck in the top-left corner and makes the body copy small. Its bottle is nearly cropped top and bottom, the CTA floats on the green circle, and there is dead space under the centred text block, so the hierarchy and the brand both feel weaker.

A rearranges the headline into four large, well-weighted lines that use the portrait width, with the CTA grouped below on the same center axis. Its only flaws are minor: the block sits low, with about 170px above the headline but only about 50px below the CTA, and 'Bubbles,' stands alone on the first line. B keeps the banner's line breaks at a timid size jammed into the top, leaves a large unexplained gap between the headline and the CTA, and leaves the bottom ~35% of the canvas empty, so it looks lopsided and unfinished.

A fills the canvas with a strong, readable headline, but its left edges don't line up (the headline starts at about x=64 while the logo and subhead start at about x=76). The headline also runs almost to the right edge with very little margin, and the CTA floats on its own on the right between the subhead and the chips, which spreads the reading order around. B has a cleaner single left edge and a sensible order (logo, headline, subhead, chips, CTA), but the headline wraps and leaves 'here' alone on its own line. All of B's content is packed into the top-left quarter, leaving the bottom-left and right half as dead space with only the decorative pink circle, so the layout is lopsided and the original's left-to-right feel is lost.

A breaks the product art. The cream circle has come loose and sits in the bottom-left corner touching the edge, and the can has lost its fill, so only an outline remains. The NEW badge floats alone in the top-right, away from the copy. B keeps the product art intact but crams everything into the top 40%, leaving the bottom 60% empty. Its Try It button is jammed against the right edge, almost touching the NEW badge and the headline. B is slightly less bad because the brand imagery survives.

A: the headline is strong and nothing collides, but the RSVP CTA has shrunk to a small pill the same size as the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS badges, so the CTA is buried. The three middle columns (tagline, date, URL) are ragged, and the legal text and URL are tiny. B: the centred headline and the large RSVP button give a clear hierarchy, but the right column is jammed against the edge: the FREE ENTRY and ALL AGES badges overlap, ALL AGES is clipped off the canvas, and the missing-asset box collides with the date. The legal text floats in the middle and the left third is dead space. A wins narrowly because it has no collisions or clipping.

A has a clear split: the book over confetti on the left and a card on the right with a dominant headline, readable body copy and the CTA paired with its fine print. Its flaws are a tiny, barely legible Inkwell & Lantern logo jammed into the card's corner, fine print nearly as big as the body copy, and a small book floating loose in the confetti. B is broken: the CTA is pushed against the bottom-left edge and runs over the fine print, which is cut off ('n the café go to…'). Its eyebrow is set oversized and over-spaced so it competes with the headline, and the book is crammed into the top-left corner.

A rearranges the design for the tall format. The bag is large, the stack is centred, and the circles are kept in proportion. Its flaws are minor: 'fizz' is orphaned on its own line, and the CTA sits slightly tight under the headline. B squeezes logo, bag, headline and CTA into the top half and leaves the bottom ~45% as dead space. Its green circle is stretched into an ellipse, which distorts the brand shape. The bag is shrunk, and the 'Find a Store' label is tiny.

A works as a left-to-right banner: the can in its circle sits on the left, a large headline in the middle and badges plus CTA on the right, with clear hierarchy. However, the GLACIER wordmark floats centred above the headline column instead of lining up with its left edge, the badges and CTA are oversized and float in their own column away from the copy, and the far right margin is uneven. B stacks everything into one cramped left column, leaving roughly 45% of the canvas on the right as dead space. Its headline is shrunk so it barely outranks the body copy, the gaps are uneven (a big gap under the headline, then tight gaps between body, badges and CTA), and the CTA and circle crowd the bottom edge.

A shrinks the headline to one thin line running almost edge to edge and pushes the LIMITED badge and CTA into the bottom-left corner. The badge and CTA are stacked under the headline but no longer align with it as one group, and the right two-thirds of the lower canvas is left empty, so the composition is lopsided and the original centered axis is gone. B keeps the original's centered headline, a strong two-line headline and the badge-plus-CTA pairing, so it is faithful and balanced. Its flaws: the tiny LIMITED badge is cramped and hard to read, the badge-plus-CTA group sits off the headline's center axis, and the gap between the headline and the CTA is tight compared with the empty space below.

A crams the whole design into the top half and leaves a huge dead area from y≈400 to 600. The product is shrunk, the CTA text and 'SINGLE ORIGIN' are tiny, and the green circle is squashed into an oval that sits beside the bag instead of behind it. B fills the story format with a large product, a strong headline and a full-size CTA, and its circles keep their proportions. Its flaws: 'fizz' is orphaned on its own line, the CTA sits too tight under the headline, and the space under the button is lopsided.

A stacks the original's portrait text column into the left half, which leaves the right ~40% of the banner dead. The headline is undersized for the format, the gap between headline and body is uneven, and the circle nearly touches the top and bottom edges. B spreads into a real left-to-right banner (product, then a large headline and body, then badges and CTA), so the hierarchy is stronger. Its flaws: the GLACIER wordmark floats centred over the gutter instead of aligning with the headline column, the body copy sits jammed near the bottom edge, and the circle also crowds the canvas edges.

A keeps the original's centred composition with a strong two-line headline and the LIMITED tag and CTA paired beneath it, as in the original. Its flaws are minor: the block sits high, with about 30px above the headline against roughly 75px of empty space below the CTA. B mixes alignments: the headline is centred on one line while the tag and CTA are pushed hard left and stacked. The headline is shrunk and loses its weight, the tag is enlarged until it competes with the CTA, and the right two-thirds of the lower half is dead space, so the layout looks lopsided and unintentional.

A has a sensible banner structure: logo and big headline on the left, the ribbon in the centre, CTA on the right. Its flaws are a tiny product bottle crammed into the top-right corner against a background circle, fine print almost as large as the subcopy, and a right column that feels cramped next to the airy left. B stretches the ribbon into a huge diagonal bar across the whole canvas that runs into the bottle and nearly touches the headline. Its logo is tiny, the fine print is minuscule and wraps to an orphaned 'Co., 2026.', and the lower right is dead space.

A: the headline crashes into the product's base and sits on top of the circle. The FREE DELIVERY badge is stranded in the bottom-left corner, the pills and CTA have shrunk to tiny sizes, and the whole bottom third of the canvas is dead space. B: a clean vertical stack with no collisions, but the alignment is mixed: GROVE is centred, the headline and body are left-aligned, and the pills and CTA are pushed right and jammed against the right edge with almost no margin, so it needs alignment fixes before shipping.

A rearranges for the square: a large four-line headline fills the canvas with strong hierarchy. However, the subhead is wrapped into a cramped, centre-rag three-line block that sits awkwardly beside the CTA in the bottom row and doesn't line up with the headline's centre axis, and the bottom row feels squeezed toward the lower edge. B is a faithful centred stack, but it is basically the original shrunk: the headline runs nearly edge to edge with thin side margins, the subhead leaves a widowed 'flavours.' on its own line, the headline-to-subhead gap is loose, and there is a lot of dead orange above and below, so it reads as an undersized copy rather than a square layout.

A crams everything into the top 55% and leaves the bottom ~45% of the canvas empty. The circle has shrunk and sits on the bottle cap like a balloon, "WEEKEND ONLY" is jammed against the top edge, and the body copy wraps into a narrow column with an orphaned "sparkling." B uses the tall format properly with a clear headline → product → CTA order and a large CTA. Its flaws: "WEEKEND ONLY" has moved below the body copy, so the eyebrow is out of order; the headline overlaps the decorative circle; and the bottle sits a little tight on the copy above it.

A: the 'Online Only' badge sits right on top of the 'Try It' button, so the call to action can't be read; the button's edges look torn, the phone's circle backdrop has mostly vanished, and the bottom third of the canvas is empty. B keeps every element whole and readable with a strong headline and CTA, but it is cramped: the phone circle is cut off at the left edge, the button and badge are jammed against the bottom-right corner, and the badge almost touches the subline.

A is just the banner row pasted into the top of a taller canvas. The bottom ~40% is empty orange, the 'Try It' button is jammed against the right edge and floats unaligned, and 'Out now.' drifts far below the headline. B rearranges the design: headline on the left, product and CTA on the right. But the CTA pill is oversized and almost touches the product circle, and 'Out now.' is stuck next to the button as an orphan instead of sitting under the headline. The headline is also somewhat small against the large product disc.

A stretches the decorative sun circle into a huge distorted oval that fills the canvas. It also floats the can alone in a dead middle band, leaving a big gap between the subtitle and the date block, which breaks the reading flow. B keeps the circle in proportion and keeps the original's order and grouping. However, B is essentially the original cropped into the new shape: the bottom third is empty, the circle sits behind the left half of the title, and both candidates show the broken 'missing asset' placeholder.

A: the red ribbon is stretched across almost the whole canvas and overlaps the headline and the bottle cap, the bottle is shrunk and jammed against the left edge, and the legal text floats ragged at the bottom right, so the layout reads as collisions rather than intent. B: a sensible left-to-right banner with the large headline on the left, the CTA with its supporting copy and legal text grouped on the right, and the logo and ribbon kept intact; but the product bottle is shrunk into the top-right corner, where it crowds the decorative circle and loses its role as the hero, and the legal text sits close to the bottom edge.

A: a clean top-to-bottom stack with the hero circle, then GROVE, then the headline. Its flaws: the left-aligned text block clashes with the right-aligned pills and CTA, and the pills nearly touch each other and run to the right canvas edge. B: the headline is overprinted on the product image and the circle, and the circle runs off the left edge. The bottom ~40% of the canvas is empty except for the stray FREE DELIVERY badge in the corner. The pills and CTA are shrunk to tiny sizes and GROVE is minuscule, so B is unusable.

A keeps the original's centred stack and colours, but the headline is small for the square, so there are large empty bands at the top and bottom. The subcopy wraps and leaves 'flavours.' alone on its own line, and the gap between headline and subcopy is too wide. B's 4-line headline fills the square and dominates well. Its bottom row is weak, though: the centre-aligned 3-line subcopy sits awkwardly beside the CTA, and the CTA's right edge (~698px) runs past the headline's edge (~640px), so they share no grid. That row is also squeezed close to the headline and the bottom edge. B is less faithful to the original's single-column flow.

A rebuilds the layout as a sensible vertical stack with a large bottle and a centred CTA. Its flaws: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow now sits below the body copy, which breaks the reading order; the body copy wraps to leave an orphaned 'sparkling.'; and the headline runs half onto the peach circle. B jams every element into the top ~55% and leaves the bottom ~45% as dead space. Its circle sits directly on the bottle cap, so the bottle reads like a balloon-headed figure, and '20% off' butts against the circle. The eyebrow is jammed near the top edge and the left copy column is cramped.

A keeps every element readable with a clear headline, subhead and CTA order. Its flaws: the phone is cropped at the left and bottom edges, the CTA button sits tight against the bottom right edge, and the badge and CTA are packed into the bottom right while the right half of the top row is empty. B is unusable: the 'ONLINE ONLY' badge collides with the 'Try It' button, which is clipped and unreadable, and a large empty band runs across the bottom and right.

A has a clear two-column structure with headline left and product right, but the Try It pill butts into the bottom of the product circle, the 'Out now.' line has been pulled away from the headline and left dangling beside the button, and the headline is undersized with dead space below it. B looks like the strip banner pasted at the top: the bottom ~40% of the canvas is empty, the Try It button is jammed against the right edge and floats loose between the headline and subline, and 'Out now.' sits far below its headline.

A is basically a scaled copy of the original. The sun circle has been enlarged so it now runs under the left of the 'Sunset Sessions' headline and the logo area, and the content is packed into the top two-thirds, leaving the bottom fifth mostly empty apart from a broken placeholder box. B stretches the round sun into a huge distorted ellipse that fills the whole canvas, which loses the original's look, and it leaves an awkward empty gap between the subhead and the date block while the can floats on its own far from the details. Both carry the 'missing asset' placeholder, but B's distorted brand shape is the worse flaw.

A keeps a sensible left-to-right order (brand, headline, copy, badges, CTA), but the backdrop circle is stretched into a distorted full-width ellipse, the can is tiny and clipped at the top edge, the CTA is jammed against the right edge, and the body copy is very small. B scrambles the reading order. SOLSTICE sits below the headline, and the CTA comes before the badges with tiny body text after them. The can is split away from its circle, leaving an empty orphan circle at the left and the can isolated at the right. There are also large dead zones, the headline crowds the top edge, and the CTA is undersized.

A: the two-line headline is jammed against the top and bottom edges, and a large dead gap sits between the phone and the text. The 'Back by Demand' badge is the same size as the CTA and stacked directly above it, so it competes with the CTA. 'Summer Only' is stranded on its own with empty space to its right, and the subline is tiny. B: the one-line headline, subline, badge pair and CTA form a cleaner, better-balanced row that reads left to right. Its flaws: the 'SOLSTICE' wordmark floats on its own next to the phone instead of sitting with the headline, the green circle is clipped at the bottom edge, and the subline and phone screen are small.

A restacks the design properly for a tall format (headline, then CTA, then product, then footer) with a strong hierarchy, but '20% off' runs almost to the right edge and the full-width pill CTA looks heavy; the purple circle sitting behind the headline reads as intentional layering. B takes the original's landscape cluster, shrinks it and parks it in the top half, leaving the bottom ~45% as dead space with the footer stranded at the bottom; the copy is too small for the canvas, and the product and circle crowd the headline and CTA.

A: the headline is readable and the colours are right, but the bottle-in-circle is a small crop jammed into the top-left corner. The NEW badge and Try It button are oversized and right-aligned, leaving left-aligned type above them with a dead lower-left quadrant, so the badge competes with the CTA. B: the white headline sits on the cream circle with almost no contrast and is nearly unreadable. The oversized bottle dominates the frame and spills below the circle, and the tiny buttons are under-weighted, so the hierarchy is broken despite a nicer composition idea.

A reads properly as a banner, left to right: brand and headline sit on the circle, then date, chips and CTA, then the phone. Its flaws are a crowded middle column, a date line that doesn't share a left edge with the chips and CTA, legal text squeezed against the bottom edge, and the placeholder image stuck awkwardly at the far right. B is clearly broken: the RSVP button and the chip row overlap the phone graphic, the large empty circle on the left wastes about a quarter of the canvas, the date and legal text are crammed at the bottom under the headline, and the placeholder is jammed into the top-right corner.

A is broken: the white headline sits right on top of the lime circle and the shoe, so it is barely readable; the logo overlaps the top of the circle; and the bottom ~45% of the canvas is empty purple. The NEW VIDEO badge has also been moved down under the subcopy, as if it were the button. B is a clean vertical stack (logo and badge, then headline, then circle and shoe, then subcopy) with nothing colliding. Its flaws are small: the shoe nearly touches the edges of the circle, 'Full review inside.' is small and pushed close to the bottom edge, and the badge sits a little tight to the top right corner.

A breaks up the design: the green circle is cut off at the left edge and sits far from the can, which has drifted to the right. The CTA has shrunk to a pill the same size as the badges, and it is jammed on the left with tiny, cramped body copy beside it, so the action is buried. B stretches the circle into a distorted ellipse that runs behind the whole banner, the can is tiny and crammed at the left edge, and the body copy is hard to read. Even so, B reads left to right from brand to headline to badges, and it ends on a CTA that clearly stands out, so its hierarchy is better.

A reads clearly left to right: phone, then a one-line headline with subtitle, then badges over the CTA. Its flaws are the SOLSTICE wordmark floating on its own between the phone and the headline, a phone shrunk almost to an icon, and badges that are nearly as heavy as the CTA. B is worse. SOLSTICE is jammed against the headline and doesn't line up with its left edge. The subtitle is tiny and hard to read. The BACK BY DEMAND badge is blown up to the same size and weight as the Find It Near You button, so the badge and CTA compete. SUMMER ONLY drifts off on its own, and there is dead space between the phone and the copy.

A squeezes the whole original layout into the top half and leaves roughly 45% of the canvas as dead lavender above a stranded legal line, so it reads like a shrunk copy, not a rearrangement; the can is also jammed against the headline column. B restacks the design properly for the tall format (headline, subhead, CTA, product, legal) and fills the canvas, but the circle now sits behind 'WEEKEND ONLY' and '20% off' instead of the product, the legal line is set nearly as large as the subhead, and the bottom footer and the product spacing are a little uneven.

A: the white serif headline sits on the cream circle, so the most important text almost disappears (a critical contrast failure), even though the large bottle and stacked NEW/Try It pills are well composed. B: the headline is bold and readable, but the bottle is shrunk to a tiny thumbnail jammed against the top edge, with a stray clipped decorative circle behind it. The NEW and Try It pills are oversized, have different widths and ragged left edges, and leave a dead empty block at bottom-left. B is flawed but usable; A's headline isn't readable.

A has real collisions: the RSVP button and the badge pills sit on top of the phone graphic, which is also cropped behind them. The decorative circle is left as an empty blob on the left, the legal line is microscopic, and the CTA and date details are split between two distant columns. B is a readable three-column banner (brand and headline / date, badges, CTA / phone) with no overlap on the CTA. Its flaws: the headline is jammed against the left edge, the middle column is cramped, the legal text is tiny, and the placeholder image crowds the phone's edge.

A is a clean vertical restack (logo and badge on top, headline, then the circle with the shoe, then the subline), with clear hierarchy and good fidelity. It has small flaws: the circle and shoe crowd the 'Full review inside.' line, the badge is nudged away from the right edge, and the logo is small. B is broken: the white headline sits right on top of the lime circle and the shoe image, so it is barely readable; the wordmark collides with the circle; the 'NEW VIDEO' badge is moved below the subline as if it were a CTA; and the bottom ~45% of the canvas is empty.
